data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The consensus probability tends to 0, but NOT through pre-existing static obstructions \u2014 through a dynamical phase transition in the cut-descent itself: as n grows, the descent from a random coloring on a random 3-regular graph enters a critical coarsening regime where the cut density converges to a positive fixed point \u03c1* \u2248 0.08, because on a 3-regular graph a vertex with a 2-1 neighbor split has its two majority neighbors of the OTHER color with probability exactly equal to the probability of the reverse \u2014 majority-3 descent is an UNBIASED walk in cut density at leading order, so there is no drift toward consensus; instead the cut density performs an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-like process around a metastable \u03c1* > 0, and absorption at 0 has probability exp(-\u0398(\u221an)) \u2192 0. The obstruction structures are not finite: they are an extensive condensate of stable single-edge cuts forming a percolating 'stripe' pattern; the prevalence of single-edge stable cuts in the FINAL state is \u0398(n) with density \u03c1*, and the consensus probability is exp(-\u0398(\u221an)).","counterconditions":[{"case":"Proof of a nonzero drift in cut density toward 0 at leading order (would restore candidate 1/3-style consensus whp)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Simulation showing final cut density \u2192 0 with n rather than stabilizing at \u03c1* > 0","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Demonstration that the OU picture's metastable density is actually absorbing-inaccessible (unstable fixed point)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Compute the drift exactly: on a 3-regular graph with local tree-like structure, condition on a vertex having neighborhood split 2-1. Its flip probability depends on correlation between its color and the configuration two steps out; at the random-coloring fixed point of the dynamics these correlations are symmetric under color exchange, so the net drift in crossing-edge density is zero to first order \u2014 unlike majority-5 or complete-graph majority where consensus is a drift-dominated flow. Second-order terms (from cycles and local clustering) create a weak restoring force toward \u03c1* > 0 but none toward 0. Hence the cut density is a mean-reverting process on [0, 1/2] with mean \u03c1* > 0, and reaching 0 requires a fluctuation of size \u03c1* against the restoring force \u2014 a large deviation of probability exp(-\u0398(\u221an)) by OU/arcsine scaling of density fluctuations. This is the zero-temperature majority-vote analogue of the known non-conservation of one-dimensional voter-model interfaces, lifted to the Bethe-lattice geometry where local equilibrium sustains a positive-interface fixed point. Final states are locally stable single-edge-cut condensates with density \u03c1* n.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
